features.name: Amazon EFS Elastic throughput mode
features.quote: Elastic Throughput is ideal for spiky and unpredictable workloads with performance requirements that are difficult to forecast.
features.predecessor: EFS Provisioned or Bursting throughput mode

features.name: Amazon EFS Archive storage class
features.quote: With EFS Archive, you now have a cost-effective way to retain even your coldest data so that it’s always available to power new business insights.
features.predecessor: EFS Standard with lifecycle management to EFS Infrequent Access (IA) as the coldest tier

features.name: Amazon FSx for OpenZFS Intelligent-Tiering storage class
features.quote: With FSx Intelligent-Tiering, customers no longer need to provision or manage storage and get automatic storage cost optimization as data access patterns change.
features.predecessor: FSx for OpenZFS SSD storage class with provisioned SSD capacity

features.name: AWS DataSync Enhanced mode
features.quote: With Enhanced mode, you can transfer datasets with virtually unlimited numbers of objects at higher levels of performance than Basic mode.
features.predecessor: A DataSync task in Basic mode, for example with an on-premises agent

features.name: AWS Transfer Family web apps
features.quote: With Transfer Family web apps, you can provide your workforce with a fully managed, branded, and secure portal for your end users to browse, upload, and download data in S3.
features.predecessor: A Transfer Family SFTP server or a custom-built web portal for browser access to S3

features.name: AWS DataSync Azure Blob Storage location
features.quote: Using DataSync, you can move your object data at scale from Azure Blob Storage to AWS Storage services such as Amazon S3.
features.predecessor: Copying Azure Blob Storage data with AzCopy or custom scripts, or a device-based transfer

features.name: S3 applies SSE-S3 by default to all new objects
features.quote: With this update, Amazon S3 will automatically apply SSE-S3 as the base level of Default Encryption setting for all new buckets and for existing buckets without any customer configured encryption setting.
patterns: \bSSE-S3\b[^\n]{0,100}\b(by default|automatically|base level|all new objects|every new object|already (encrypts?|applied))
features.predecessor: Turning on default bucket encryption or a bucket policy that denies unencrypted PutObject requests

features.name: AWS KMS external key store (XKS)
features.quote: XKS may help you address your compliance needs where encryption keys for regulated workloads must be outside AWS and solely under your control.
features.predecessor: A KMS custom key store backed by AWS CloudHSM, or importing key material into KMS

features.name: S3 blocks SSE-C by default on new buckets
features.quote: In April 2026, Amazon S3 deployed an update so all new general purpose buckets have SSE-C encryption disabled for all new write requests.
features.predecessor: SSE-C usable on any new bucket without an opt-in

features.name: Dual-layer server-side encryption with KMS keys (DSSE-KMS)
features.quote: Dual-layer server-side encryption with keys stored in AWS Key Management Service (DSSE-KMS) is designed to meet National Security Agency CNSSP 15 for FIPS compliance and Data-at-Rest Capability Package (DAR CP) Version 5.0 guidance for two layers of CNSA encryption.
features.predecessor: SSE-KMS (one layer) combined with client-side encryption before upload to get two layers

features.name: Multiple MFA devices per IAM user and root user
features.quote: Now it is possible to add up to eight MFA devices per user, including FIDO security keys, software time-based one-time password (TOTP) with virtual authenticator applications, or hardware TOTP tokens.
features.predecessor: A single MFA device per IAM user, with account recovery if the device is lost

features.name: Passkeys as an MFA method for IAM and root users
features.quote: IAM now allows you to secure access to AWS accounts using passkeys for multi-factor authentication (MFA) with support for built-in authenticators, such as Touch ID on Apple MacBooks and Windows Hello facial recognition on PCs.
features.predecessor: FIDO U2F security keys, virtual (TOTP) or hardware TOTP MFA devices

features.name: Centralized root access management for member accounts
features.quote: Now, administrators can remove unnecessary root credentials for member accounts in AWS Organizations and then, if needed, perform tightly scoped privileged actions using temporary credentials.
features.predecessor: Securing the root user of each member account individually (password, MFA, access keys) and signing in as root for tasks

features.name: S3 Block Public Access organization-level policy in AWS Organizations
features.quote: S3 Block Public Access at the organization level uses a single configuration that controls all public access settings across accounts within your organization.
features.predecessor: Account-level S3 Block Public Access in each account, protected by an SCP

features.name: AWS Lake Formation hybrid access mode
features.quote: With the Hybrid Access Mode, you now have an incremental path wherein you can enable Lake Formation for a specific set of users without interrupting other existing users or workloads.
features.predecessor: Moving every principal to Lake Formation permissions at once, or keeping IAM and S3 bucket policies

features.name: AWS Lambda SnapStart
features.quote: Lambda SnapStart offers improved startup times by initializing the function’s code ahead of time, taking a snapshot of the initialized execution environment, and caching it.
features.predecessor: Lambda provisioned concurrency to keep execution environments initialized

features.name: Amazon EKS Auto Mode
features.quote: Amazon EKS Auto Mode simplifies running Kubernetes by offloading cluster operations to AWS, improves the performance and security of your applications, and helps optimize compute costs.
features.predecessor: EKS managed node groups or self-managed nodes with Cluster Autoscaler or Karpenter that you operate

features.name: Lambda maximum concurrency for an SQS event source mapping
features.quote: Maximum Concurrency for SQS as an event source allows customers to control the maximum concurrent invokes by the Amazon SQS event source.
features.predecessor: Function-level reserved concurrency to throttle SQS consumption

features.name: EC2 Auto Scaling instance refresh rollback (including automatic rollback on alarms)
features.quote: With today’s launch, you can use rollback to undo changes an instance refresh made when it fails.
features.predecessor: Instance refresh or a CloudFormation rolling update without rollback, so a failed rollout is reverted by hand

features.name: ALB target group health requirements (minimum healthy targets, DNS failover and routing failover)
features.quote: This release adds support to configure the minimum count or percentage of targets that must be healthy, and what actions the load balancer takes when the threshold is not met.
features.predecessor: Route 53 health checks and failover routing in front of the load balancer

features.name: Amazon S3 Express One Zone
features.quote: S3 Express One Zone can improve data access speeds by 10x and reduce request costs by 50% compared to S3 Standard.
features.predecessor: S3 Standard (or S3 One Zone-IA) general purpose buckets

features.name: AWS KMS on-demand key rotation and custom rotation periods
features.quote: You can now customize the frequency of rotation period between 90 days to 7 years (2560 days) as well as invoke key rotation on demand for customer managed KMS keys.
features.predecessor: Automatic annual KMS rotation, or creating a new key and repointing the alias to rotate immediately

features.name: AWS Secrets Manager managed external secrets
features.quote: At launch, managed external secrets feature is available for 3 listed partners — Salesforce, BigID and Snowflake.
features.predecessor: A custom rotation Lambda function that rotates the SaaS provider secret

features.name: S3 Lifecycle default minimum object size of 128 KB for transitions
features.quote: While the object size filter for your existing S3 Lifecycle rules will not automatically change, this new default behavior will be applied to any new or modified S3 Lifecycle configuration.
features.predecessor: Lifecycle transition rules applied to all objects, including very small ones, with no size default

features.name: AWS Direct Connect native 400 Gbps dedicated connections
features.quote: Native 400 Gbps connections provide higher bandwidth, without the operational overhead of managing multiple 100 Gbps connections in a link aggregation group.
features.predecessor: A LAG of several 100 Gbps (or smaller) dedicated connections

features.name: AWS Backup cold storage tier for Amazon EBS snapshots (EBS Snapshots Archive)
features.quote: You can now use AWS Backup to transition your EBS Snapshots to EBS Snapshots Archive and manage their lifecycle, alongside AWS Backup’s other supported resources.
features.predecessor: EBS backups kept in warm storage only (or EBS snapshots in the standard tier)

preGuide.name: S3 Batch Replication for existing objects
preGuide.quote: Now, with S3 Batch Replication, you can synchronize existing objects between buckets.
preGuide.predecessor: Live replication (SRR or CRR) for new objects only, plus S3 Batch Operations copy or sync

preGuide.name: AWS Organizations backup policies applied to resources by tag
preGuide.quote: You can use backup policies to create and enforce backup policies across all of the accounts in your organization.
preGuide.predecessor: Backup plans configured account by account

notes: Group A. All dates come from the "Posted On" line of the cited AWS What's New page (cached page text), except ALB target group health (doc-history entry dated November 28, 2022, not 2023-11 as the candidate list guessed) and SSE-C (FAQ says April 2026, month only). S3 Batch Replication for existing objects (2022-02-08), Organizations backup policies by tag (2020-07-08, Organizations document history) and AWS Backup hourly frequency (long-standing cron/console option, no dated post found, unconfirmed) are before the cutoff and are in preGuide. KMS on-demand rotation: the standard-key feature launched 2024-04-12 together with custom rotation periods (06/2025 post is the imported-key extension only). DataSync Azure Blob: preview 2023-03-29, GA July 2023. EBS cold storage: What's New 2023-11-27; Backup doc history lists 2023-12-18. ALB: both the 2023 candidate guess and the NLB equivalent (2022-11-17) were wrong. The backup-ebs-cold-storage and backup-hourly patterns use multi-line spans because the stem and options are joined by newlines. Patterns for generic terms (provisioned concurrency, SSE-C, S3 Standard) appear only as predecessorPatterns.
